title: RateGuard: Distributed Rate Limiter with Redis, Lua and an AI Policy Advisor
tagline: Build a multi-tenant rate-limiting service whose limits hold across every instance, survive a Redis outage and never over-admit, with AI as your pair programmer
description: Over nine phases you build RateGuard like a professional team: requirements and threats, design with ADRs, a test-first implementation of a token bucket and a sliding window counter as pure functions and as atomic Redis Lua scripts that use one clock, a Redis Cluster-ready key layout with hash tags, tenants with SHA-256 hashed API keys and a constant-time admin token, the standard rate-limit headers and Retry-After, per-minute usage statistics and an AI policy advisor with an offline fallback, integration tests that race parallel requests for the last token, CI/CD with GitHub Actions, Docker, optional free-tier deployment, a game day that freezes Redis, a circuit breaker with per-tenant fail modes, observability and a retrospective. Pick Java, Python or TypeScript; the spec, the Lua scripts and the tests are shared. Everything runs on your laptop, and the AI feature works offline.

prerequisites.title: Git and the command line basics
One of: Java, Python or TypeScript fundamentals
REST APIs and HTTP status codes
Basic concurrency: what a race condition is

outcomes: Turn a multi-tenant API brief into testable requirements, user stories and a threat list (stolen keys, over-admission across instances, key-pattern injection, retry storms)
Compare rate-limiting algorithms and implement a token bucket and a sliding window counter as pure, exhaustively tested functions
Make limiter decisions atomic across instances with Redis Lua scripts, one clock (Redis TIME) and parity tests against the pure functions
Design a Redis key layout that is Redis Cluster ready (hash tags), expires idle state and never uses KEYS
Secure a service with hashed, rotatable API keys and a constant-time admin token, and prove every refusal with tests
Add an AI policy advisor whose output is validated, never auto-applied and falls back to deterministic rules offline
Build CI/CD with GitHub Actions: matrix, caching, reusable workflows, Redis service containers, GHCR
Run a game day that freezes Redis, write a blameless post-mortem and add a circuit breaker with per-tenant fail modes
Add request IDs, JSON logs and metrics, and keep v1.0 and v1.1 data compatible both ways
Use AI assistants deliberately and verify every output
ai_feature: AI policy advisor: reads a tenant's per-minute usage statistics and suggests KEEP, RAISE_LIMIT, LOWER_LIMIT or INVESTIGATE with a plain-language summary. Offline deterministic rules by default, optional Ollama or a free Gemini/Groq key; the output is validated, never applied automatically, and no rate-limit decision depends on the AI
portfolio_blurb: Built RateGuard, a multi-tenant distributed rate limiter: token bucket and sliding window counter as pure functions and as atomic Redis Lua scripts (parity-tested, Redis TIME as the only clock), proven by parallel requests across instances to never over-admit; a Redis Cluster-ready key layout with hash tags; SHA-256 hashed, rotatable API keys; standard rate-limit headers; an AI policy advisor with validated output and offline fallback; >=85 % test coverage; GitHub Actions CI/CD to GHCR; Docker; and, after a game day that froze Redis, a circuit breaker with per-tenant fail modes (closed, open, local), request IDs, JSON logs and metrics.
